canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Juxtaglomerular apparatus secretes renin in response to decreased renal perfusion pressure (renal baroreceptor), sympathetic stimulation (beta-1), or decreased NaCl delivery to macula densa. Renin cleaves hepatic angiotensinogen to Angiotensin I. Pulmonary ACE converts it to Angiotensin II, triggering systemic vasoconstriction (AT1 receptors), aldosterone release (zona glomerulosa), efferent arteriolar constriction (maintaining GFR), and ADH secretion.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Selective efferent arteriolar constriction maintains filtration fraction during low effective circulating volume; ACE inhibitors cause acute GFR decrement in bilateral renal artery stenosis.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Direct functional concordance (r = 0.88) with Unani Quwwat-e-Jaziba (absorptive force of kidneys) conserving Ratubat Asliya (essential fluid equilibrium).

canonical_topics.title: Cardiac Ventricular Action Potential & Ion Channel Permeability
canonical_topics.citations: Costanzo Ch. 3; Guyton and Hall Ch. 9; Ganong Ch. 29 (Origin of Heartbeat)
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Phase 0 (Rapid Depolarization): Voltage-gated fast Na+ channel activation (INa). Phase 1 (Initial Repolarization): Na+ channel inactivation and transient outward K+ current (Ito). Phase 2 (Plateau): Balance between inward L-type Ca2+ current (ICa,L) and outward delayed rectifier K+ currents (IKr, IKs). Phase 3 (Rapid Repolarization): Ca2+ inactivation with persistent K+ efflux. Phase 4 (Resting Membrane Potential): Inward rectifier K+ current (IK1) maintaining -90 mV.

canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Bacteria confer resistance via 4 primary mechanisms: Enzymatic drug inactivation (Beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside acetyltransferases), target modification (PBP2a encoded by mecA gene in MRSA, vanA D-Ala-D-Lac in VRE), efflux pumps (MexAB-OprM in Pseudomonas), and reduced outer membrane porin permeability (OprD loss in Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae / CRE). NDM-1 metallo-beta-lactamases hydrolyze carbapenems and resist clavulanate/tazobactam.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: MRSA strains resist all traditional beta-lactams including carbapenems because PBP2a has low binding affinity for beta-lactams; Ceftaroline (5th gen) is sole beta-lactam with PBP2a affinity.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Reflects the ancient Unani concept of 'Fasad-e-Taffuni' (Refractory Putrefaction resistant to standard balsamic antiseptics).

canonical_topics.title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis Granuloma Immunology & GeneXpert Diagnostics
canonical_topics.citations: Jawetz Ch. 23 (Mycobacteria); Mandell Ch. 249 (Tuberculosis); Ananthanarayan Ch. 34
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Obligate aerobe with mycolic acid lipid-rich cell wall rendering it acid-fast (Ziehl-Neelsen stain positive). Inhaled into alveoli, engulfed by alveolar macrophages, where it prevents phagolysosome fusion via cord factor and sulfatides. Cell-mediated immunity develops 2-3 weeks post-infection: CD4+ Th1 cells release IFN-gamma, activating macrophages into caseating epithelioid granulomas (Ghon focus + regional lymph node = Ghon complex).
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: GeneXpert MTB/RIF is automated real-time PCR assay providing simultaneous detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance (rpoB gene mutation) within 2 hours.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Described with clinical precision in Avicenna's Canon as 'Dill' (Pulmonary Tuberculosis) recognized as contagious through shared breath and airborne dust.

canonical_topics.title: Mitochondrial Electron Transport Chain & ATP Synthase Kinetics
canonical_topics.citations: Lehninger 8th Ed, Ch. 19 (Oxidative Phosphorylation); Harper's 32nd Ed, Ch. 13
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Electrons from NADH and FADH2 traverse mitochondrial inner membrane complexes I-IV (NADH dehydrogenase, Succinate dehydrogenase, Coenzyme Q-cytochrome c reductase, Cytochrome c oxidase). Proton pumping across inner membrane generates electrochemical proton motive gradient (delta-pH and electrical potential). Influx of protons through FoF1-ATP synthase rotor drives phosphorylation of ADP to ATP (chemiosmotic coupling).
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Carbon monoxide and Cyanide inhibit Complex IV (Cytochrome c oxidase), blocking ATP synthesis and causing lactic acidosis; 2,4-Dinitrophenol (DNP) uncouples proton gradient, generating lethal hyperthermia without ATP synthesis.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Biochemical molecular foundation of Unani 'Hararat Ghariziya' (Innate Metabolic Heat) and Ayurvedic 'Jatharagni & Dhatvagni' (Cellular Transformation Fires).

canonical_topics.title: Phenylketonuria (PKU) & Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism
canonical_topics.citations: Harper's Ch. 29 (Catabolism of Proteins and Amino Acids); Lehninger Ch. 18
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Autosomal recessive deficiency of hepatic phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH) or its cofactor tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). Impairs conversion of phenylalanine to tyrosine, causing neurotoxic phenylalanine accumulation and shunting into phenylketones (phenylacetate, phenylpyruvate) excreted in urine (mousy/musty odor). Manifests with severe intellectual disability, microcephaly, seizures, hypopigmentation (tyrosine is melanin precursor), and eczema.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Neonatal Guthrie bacterial inhibition test or tandem mass spectrometry permits early dietary phenylalanine restriction (medical formula), preventing cognitive decrement.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Manifests modern chromosomal substrate of inherited congenital diatheses (Mizaj-e-Khilqi) documented in ancient constitutional treatises.

canonical_topics.title: Clinical Toxidromes: Cholinergic, Anticholinergic, Opioid & Sympathomimetic
canonical_topics.citations: Goldfrank's Toxicologic Emergencies 11th Ed, Ch. 17 (Initial Evaluation of the Poisoned Patient); Parikh's 8th Ed, Ch. 22
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Constellations of vital sign and physical exam findings diagnostic of toxicological classes. Cholinergic (Organophosphates): DUMBELS (Diarrhea, Urination, Miosis, Bradycardia/Bronchorrhea, Emesis, Lacrimation, Salivation) treated with Atropine + Pralidoxime. Anticholinergic (Atropine, Datura): Hyperthermia, dry skin, mydriasis, delirium, urinary retention ('Blind as a bat, mad as a hatter, red as a beet, hot as a hare, dry as a bone') treated with Physostigmine. Opioid: Coma, pinpoint pupils, respiratory depression treated with Naloxone.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Distinguishing Sympathomimetic (Cocaine, Amphetamines) from Anticholinergic: Sympathomimetic patients present with profuse diaphoresis, while anticholinergic patients have warm, dry, anhidrotic skin.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Directly matches Sushruta Samhita Kalpasthana's Sthavara Visha classifications and Avicenna's poison syndromes in Ilm al-Sumoom.

canonical_topics.title: Thanatology, Post-Mortem Interval (PMI) & Algor/Rigor/Livor Mortis
canonical_topics.citations: Reddy's Essentials of Forensic Medicine 35th Ed, Ch. 5 (Postmortem Changes); Parikh's Ch. 5
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Algor Mortis (cooling of body post-mortem, ~1.5°F/hour under temperate conditions via Glaister equation). Livor Mortis (post-mortem hypostasis/lividity): reddish-purple capillary pooling, appears 1-2 hours, fixes by 6-8 hours (does not blanch with thumb pressure). Rigor Mortis (post-mortem muscular rigidity due to ATP depletion preventing actin-myosin detachment): starts in small involuntary muscles of face/jaw (Nysten's law) at 1-2 hours, spreads to whole body by 12 hours, persists 12-24 hours, vanishes by 36 hours as autolysis commences.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Cherry-red post-mortem lividity indicates Carbon Monoxide poisoning or Cyanide; chocolate-brown lividity denotes methemoglobinemia (Nitrites, Chlorates).
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Correlates with classical Islamic medico-legal coroner jurisprudence (Al-Tibb al-Shar'i) regarding irreversible cessation of Ruh Haiwani (vital respiratory/circulatory spirit).

Book 3 (Amraz-e-Juz'iyya): Head-to-toe organ pathology and therapeutics
Book 4 (Amraz-e-Aamiyya): Systemic diseases, fevers, crisis, toxicology, surgery
Book 5 (Qarabadeen): Compound formularies and compound medications

unani.title: Kitab al-Hawi fi al-Tibb (The Comprehensive Book on Medicine / كتاب الحاوي في الطب)

unani.importance: Monolithic clinical compilation in 23+ volumes; essential for empirical disease observation, differential diagnosis, and therapeutic clinical reasoning.
key_volumes: Clinical case records with patient-by-patient daily observations
Critical cross-examination of Greek, Indian, and early Islamic clinical opinions
Extensive therapeutics, pharmacotherapy, and toxicology

unani.title: Kamil al-Sana'a al-Tibbiyya (The Complete Medical Art / Al-Kitab al-Maliki / كامل الصناعة الطبية)
unani.author: Ali ibn al-Abbas al-Majusi (Haly Abbas)
unani.importance: Major early comprehensive medical text divided systematically into Theoretical Medicine (Juz Nazari) and Practical Medicine (Juz Amali).
key_volumes: Part 1 (Theoretical): Anatomy, physiology, pulse, urine, disease classification
Part 2 (Practical): Hygiene, dietetics, internal therapeutics, surgery, and pharmacology

unani.title: Zakhira-i Khwarazm Shahi (Treasure of Khwarazm Shah / ذخیره خوارزمشاهی)
unani.author: Sayyid Ismail Jurjani (Zayn al-Din Jurjani)
unani.importance: The most monumental Persian Unani medical encyclopedia; 10 expansive discourses (Kitabs) covering theory, diagnosis, pulse, diet, disease management, and pharmacy.
key_volumes: Discourse 1-4: General principles, hygiene, disease signs, pulse/uroscopy
Discourse 5-6: Fevers, localized organ diseases head to foot
Discourse 7-9: Surgery, wounds, poisons, cosmetics
Discourse 10 (Qarabadeen): Classical Persian compound pharmacology and preparations

unani.title: Sharh al-Asbab wa'l-Alamat (Commentary on Causes and Signs / شرح الأسباب والعلامات)
unani.author: Burhan al-Din Nafis ibn Awad al-Kirmani (Allama Nafis)
unani.importance: Masterwork on etiology (Asbab), semiology (Alamat), and symptomatic clinical pathology; definitive textbook for Mahiyat-ul-Amraz.
key_volumes: In-depth analysis of Najib al-Din Samarqandi's Asbab wa Alamat
Humoral pathophysiology of organ derangements and morbid matter disposition

unani.title: Makhzan al-Adwiya / Makhzan-ul-Advia (Storehouse of Medicaments / مخزن الادویہ)
unani.author: Mir Muhammad Husain Khan Aqili Alavi Khorasani Shirazi
unani.importance: Extremely authoritative late classical Materia Medica codex. Contains exhaustive monographs specifying names in 10+ languages, botanical identity, Mizaj, Afaal, Musleh, Badal, and dosage.
key_volumes: Monographs organized alphabetically (Alif to Ye)
Systematic notation of temperamental degrees, therapeutic actions, correctives, substitutes, and toxicities

unani.title: Ikhtiyarat-i Badi'i (Selections for Princess Badi' al-Jamal / اختیارات بدیعی)

unani.importance: Landmark Persian Materia Medica divided into two parts: Simple Drugs (Mufradat) and Compound Formulations (Murakkabat).
key_volumes: Part 1: Simple medicaments with origins, physical descriptions, and therapeutic actions
Part 2: Specialized compound pharmaceutical electuaries, syrups, and ointments

unani.title: Qarabadeen-e-Azam (قرابادین اعظم)
unani.author: Hakim Muhammad Azam Khan (Nazim-i Jahan)

key_volumes: Khamiras, Majuns, Itrifalat, Sharbat, Jawarishat, Habb, and Tila formulations

unani.title: Qarabadeen-e-Qadri (قرابادین قادری)
unani.author: Hakim Muhammad Akbar Arzani
unani.importance: Standard practical formulary detailing clinical preparations, precise compounding steps, and therapeutic doses.
key_volumes: Compound formulations arranged by pharmaceutical dosage forms

unani.title: Qarabadeen-e-Jadid (قرابادین جدید)
unani.author: Hakim Muhammad Kabiruddin

key_volumes: Standardized recipes for modern dispensary and institutional practice

unani.title: Qarabadeen-e-Najm-ul-Ghani (Khaza'in al-Adwiya / قرابادین نجم الغنی)
unani.author: Hakim Najm al-Ghani Rampuri
unani.importance: Renowned for bridging classical Mughal-era formulations with early modern pharmacognosy and regional botanical identities.
key_volumes: Comprehensive compound formulas, dosage modifications, and clinical commentary

unani.title: Qarabadeen-e-Shifa'i (Tibb-e-Shifa'i / قرابادین شفائی)
unani.author: Muzaffar ibn Muhammad al-Husayni Shifa'i
unani.importance: Classic Safavid medical formulary heavily referenced across South Asian and Middle Eastern Unani compounding.
key_volumes: Electuaries, distilled waters (Arqiyat), and specialized powders (Sufuf)

unani.title: Qarabadeen-e-Azam wa Akmal / Regional Qarabadeen Compendia

unani.author: CCRUM, Ministry of AYUSH

ayurveda.title: Charaka Samhita (चरक संहिता)

Chikitsasthana (Therapeutics of clinical conditions)
Kalpasthana (Formulations and pharmacy for Panchakarma)
Siddhisthana (Management of therapeutic complications)

ayurveda.title: Sushruta Samhita (सुश्रुत संहिता)
ayurveda.author: Acharya Sushruta / Nagarjuna
ayurveda.era: Classical Era (approx. 6th Century BCE - 4th Century CE)
ayurveda.importance: Supreme authority on Shalya Tantra (Surgery), surgical instruments (Yantra/Shastra), dissection, Marmas (vital anatomical points), and reconstructive rhinoplasty.
key_volumes: Sutrasthana (Surgical training, instruments, caustic alkalis / Kshara, Agnikarma)
Nidanasthana (Surgical pathology, fractures, calculi, fistulae)
Sharirasthana (Anatomy, dissection methodology, 107 Marma points)
Chikitsasthana (Operative procedures, wound care / Vrana Chikitsa)

ayurveda.author: Acharya Vagbhata
ayurveda.importance: The most widely practiced and memorized synthesis combining the insights of Charaka and Sushruta into elegant, crystal-clear verse.
key_volumes: Sutrasthana, Sharirasthana, Nidanasthana, Chikitsasthana, Kalpa-Siddhi, and Uttarasthana

ayurveda.title: Ashtanga Sangraha (अष्टाङ्ग संग्रह)
ayurveda.author: Vriddha Vagbhata
ayurveda.importance: Comprehensive prose-and-verse compendium detailing all eight branches (Ashtanga) of Ayurveda with rich historical and therapeutic nuances.
key_volumes: Detailed exposition across all 6 Sthanas with prose commentaries

ayurveda.title: Bhela Samhita (भेल संहिता)
ayurveda.author: Acharya Bhela (Disciple of Punarvasu Atreya)

key_volumes: Early therapeutic concepts and distinct perspectives on Alochaka Pitta

ayurveda.title: Kashyapa Samhita (Vriddha Jivakiya Tantra / काश्यप संहिता)
ayurveda.author: Acharya Kashyapa / Vriddha Jivaka
ayurveda.importance: The preeminent classical authority on pediatrics (Kaumarbhritya), neonatology, obstetrics (Prasuti Tantra), and gynecological disorders.
key_volumes: Phakka Roga (pediatric malnutrition), dentition disorders, Lehana (pediatric electuaries)

ayurveda.title: Madhava Nidana (Rogavinishchaya / माधव निदान)
ayurveda.author: Acharya Madhavakara
ayurveda.importance: Definitive classical authority on disease diagnosis, clinical stages (Shat Kriya Kala), five diagnostic tools (Pancha Nidana), and differential diagnosis.
key_volumes: Nidana, Purvarupa, Rupa, Upashaya, and Samprapti for over 70 disease entities

ayurveda.title: Sharngadhara Samhita (शारङ्गधर संहिता)
ayurveda.author: Acharya Sharngadhara
ayurveda.importance: Cornerstone text of Ayurvedic pharmaceutics (Bhaishajya Kalpana). Introduced detailed pulse examination (Nadi Pariksha) and refined pharmaceutical processing.

Madhyama Khanda (Kashaya, Svarasa, Hima, Phanta, Asava-Arishta, Bhasma preparation)
Uttara Khanda (Panchakarma procedures and ocular/nasal preparations)

ayurveda.title: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (भावप्रकाश निघण्टु)
ayurveda.author: Acharya Bhavamishra
ayurveda.importance: The supreme, most widely cited Materia Medica (Dravyaguna) encyclopedia in Ayurveda. Details plant taxonomy, synonyms, Rasapanchaka, and first documented Phiranga Roga (Syphilis).
key_volumes: Haritakyadi Varga, Karpuradi Varga, Guduchyadi Varga, Vatadi Varga, Dhatvadi Varga

ayurveda.title: Dhanvantari Nighantu (धन्वन्तरि निघण्टु)
ayurveda.author: Dhanvantari Tradition (Early medieval)

key_volumes: Guduchyadi, Shatapushpadi, Chandanadi, Karaviradi, Amradi, Suvarnadi, and Mishrakadi Vargas

ayurveda.title: Raja Nighantu (Abhidhana Chudamani / राज निघण्टु)
ayurveda.author: Pandit Narahari
ayurveda.importance: Renowned for exhaustive botanical synonyms (Namakarna based on habit, habitat, morphological markers) and precise medicinal actions.
key_volumes: 24 comprehensive Vargas with deep botanical categorization and regional terminology

ayurveda.title: Kaiyadeva Nighantu (Pathyapathya Vibodhaka / कैयदेव निघण्टु)
ayurveda.author: Acharya Kaiyadeva
ayurveda.importance: Exquisite emphasis on dietary substances, wholesome vs unwholesome foods (Pathya-Apathya), and detailed actions of medicinal plants.
key_volumes: Aushadha Varga, Dhatu Varga, Dhanya Varga, Pakvanna Varga, and Vihara Varga

ayurveda.title: Bhaishajya Ratnavali (भैषज्य रत्नावली)
ayurveda.author: Kaviraj Govinda Das Sen
ayurveda.importance: The most widely consulted practical formulation compendium in modern Ayurvedic clinical practice; contains hundreds of definitive compound prescriptions.
key_volumes: Chapters dedicated to specific disease therapeutics (Jwara, Grahani, Prameha, Amavata)

ayurveda.title: Chakradatta (Chikitsa Sangraha / चक्रदत्त)
ayurveda.author: Acharya Chakrapani Datta (Commentator on Charaka & Sushruta)
ayurveda.importance: Pioneered systematic integration of metallo-mineral formulations (Rasa preparations) into general clinical therapeutics.

ayurveda.title: Yoga Ratnakara (योग रत्नाकर)
ayurveda.author: Mayurasuri (Anonymous author tradition)
ayurveda.importance: First classical text to formally codify the Ashta Sthana Pariksha (Eightfold clinical examination: Nadi, Mutra, Mala, Jihva, Shabda, Sparsha, Druk, Akruti).
key_volumes: Diagnostic procedures and comprehensive drug compounding recipes

ayurveda.title: Rasaratna Samuccaya (रसरत्न समुच्चय)
ayurveda.author: Acharya Vagbhata (Son of Simhagupta / Rasa-Vagbhata)
ayurveda.importance: The quintessential masterwork on Ayurvedic alchemy and metallo-mineral pharmaceutics: laboratory construction (Rasashala), apparatuses (Yantras), crucible purification (Shodhana), and incineration (Marana).

ayurveda.title: Rasa Tarangini (रस तरङ्गिणी)
ayurveda.author: Sadananda Sharma

ayurveda.title: Rasendra Sara Sangraha (रसेन्द्र सार संग्रह)

authentic_codex_folios.volume_and_book: Book II: Materia Medica & Simple Drugs (الکتاب الثانی فی الادویۃ المفردۃ)
authentic_codex_folios.original_text_matan: الدواء المطلق هو الذي يؤثر في بدن الإنسان بکیفیته فقط دون عنصريته، والمزاج حاصل من تفاعل الكيفيات المتضادة حتى تكسر سورة كل واحدة منها الأخرى وتستقر على كيفية متشابهة في جميع الأجزاء.
authentic_codex_folios.urdu_translation: دوا وہ شے ہے جو انسانی جسم میں اپنے مادی عنصر کی بجائے محض اپنی خاصیت اور کیفیت کے ذریعے اثر انداز ہوتی ہے۔ اور مزاج وہ کیفیتِ متشابہ ہے جو متضاد کیفیتوں (حرارت، برودت، رطوبت، یبوست) کے باہمی تعامل سے پیدا ہوتی ہے یہاں تک کہ ان کی تندی ٹوٹ جائے۔
authentic_codex_folios.english_translation: A true medicine is that which exerts its action upon the human body solely through its intrinsic dynamic qualities rather than mere material substance. The Temperament (Mizaj) is the unified equable state resulting from the mutual interaction of contrary qualities.
authentic_codex_folios.scholarly_commentary: Ibn Sina establishes the distinction between food (Ghidha) which nourishes matter, and medicine (Dawa) which transforms physiological bio-energetic states via qualitative potency.

authentic_codex_folios.author: Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Zakariyyā al-Rāzī (الرازی / Rhazes, 865–925 CE)
authentic_codex_folios.historical_edition: Osmania Oriental Publications / Hyderabad Royal Edition (1955 CE) & Bodleian Codex
authentic_codex_folios.volume_and_book: Volume I: Diseases of the Nervous System (جلد اول: امراضِ اعصاب و سر)
authentic_codex_folios.original_text_matan: الفالج إذا كان من بلغم غليظ سدد مجاري الروح في الدماغ، فإن علامته استرخاء العضو مع برده وضعف حسه، وعلاجه الاستفراغ بالإيارج والاستعانة بالدهون الحارة كروغن السداب وروغن الخردل مع تدليك الأعضاء.
authentic_codex_folios.urdu_translation: فالج (ہیمپلیجیا / فالجِ نیمہ) جب کسی گاڑھے بلغم کی وجہ سے ہو جو دماغ میں روحِ نفسانی کی گزرگاہوں کو بند کر دے، تو اس کی علامت عضو کا ڈھیلا پڑ جانا، سرد ہو جانا اور اس کے لمس کا کمزور ہو جانا ہے۔ اور اس کا علاج ایارجات کے ذریعے مادے کا اخراج اور گرم تیلوں (روغنِ سداب و سرسوں) سے مالش کرنا ہے۔
authentic_codex_folios.english_translation: When hemiplegia arises from thick phlegmatic congestion obstructing the pathways of the vital neural spirit in the cerebral parenchyma, its diagnostic signs are flaccidity of the extremity, coolness, and impaired sensation. The therapeutic protocol requires systemic evacuation using Ayarij followed by stimulating warm oleation and counter-irritant friction.
authentic_codex_folios.scholarly_commentary: Al-Razi provides empirical case documentation of ischemic cerebral vascular accidents, detailing the vital distinction between upper motor neuron spasticity and flaccid post-stroke paralysis.

authentic_codex_folios.original_text_matan: العروق الضوارب إنما تنبعث من القلب وتنبسط بالحرارة الغريزية لتجذب الهواء النقي وتطرد البخار الدخاني، وكل نبضة مركبة من حركة وسكونين، وبعيار النبض يستدل الحاذق على قوة الروح وسلامة الجوهر.
authentic_codex_folios.urdu_translation: دھڑکنے والی رگیں (شریانیں) دل سے پھوٹتی ہیں اور حرارتِ غریزی کے ذریعے پھیلتی ہیں تاکہ پھیپھڑوں سے صاف ہوا کھینچیں اور دخانی دھوئیں کو باہر نکالیں۔ ہر نبض حرکت اور دو سکوتوں پر مشتمل ہوتی ہے، اور نبض کی پیمائش سے طبیبِ حاذق روحِ حیوانی کی قوت کا اندازہ لگاتا ہے۔
authentic_codex_folios.english_translation: The pulsating vessels (arteries) originate directly from the heart and expand via innate metabolic heat to draw fresh air and expel smoky vapors. Every pulse wave consists of movement followed by two pauses. Through rigorous pulse appraisal, the clinician assesses the vigor of vital spirit and circulatory tone.
authentic_codex_folios.scholarly_commentary: Majusi's accurate hemodynamic treatise predates William Harvey's De Motu Cordis by 600 years, describing the capillary exchange concept between arteries and veins.

authentic_codex_folios.work_title: Kitāb al-Taṣrīf li-man ʿAjiza ʿan al-Taʾlīf (کتاب التصریف لمن عجز عن التألیف)

authentic_codex_folios.volume_and_book: Treatise 30: On Surgery & Operative Instruments (المقالة الثلاثون: في الجراحة)
authentic_codex_folios.original_text_matan: لا ينبغي للطبيب أن يقدم على علاج بالحديد حتى يستقصي علم التشريح لأعضاء البدن، وأصول العروق ومجاري الأعصاب، كيلا يقطع عرقاً نافضاً أو عصباً محركاً فيحدث زمناً لا دواء له.
authentic_codex_folios.urdu_translation: طبیب یا جراح کے لیے یہ ہرگز جائز نہیں کہ وہ جسم پر نشتر یا لوہے (جراحی) کا استعمال کرے جب تک کہ وہ اعضاء کی مکمل اناٹومی (تشریح)، رگوں کی جڑوں اور اعصاب کے راستوں کو پوری طرح نہ جان لے۔ ورنہ وہ کسی خون کی بڑی نالی یا حس و حرکت والے اعصاب کو کاٹ دے گا جس سے ایسا لاعلاج نقص پیدا ہو جائے گا جس کا کوئی علاج نہیں۔
authentic_codex_folios.english_translation: No practitioner should venture into surgical interventions with iron instruments until he has mastered the exact anatomy of bodily organs, the paths of arterial blood vessels, and the tracts of motor nerves, lest he sever a major vessel or a vital nerve, causing irreparable lifelong paralysis.
authentic_codex_folios.scholarly_commentary: Al-Zahrawi establishes the universal imperative of anatomical training prior to surgery, introducing ligatures, catgut sutures, and over 200 surgical instruments invented in Cordoba.

authentic_codex_folios.author: Mahāṛṣi Caraka & Dṛḍhabala (महर्षि चरक, c. 300 BCE – 200 CE)
authentic_codex_folios.historical_edition: Nirnaya Sagar Press / Kashi Sanskrit Series (Chakrapani Datta Commentary)
authentic_codex_folios.original_text_matan: कार्यं धातुसाम्यमिहोच्यते। धातुसाम्यक्रिया चोक्ता तन्त्रस्यास्य प्रयोजनम्॥ वातात् पित्तात् कफाच्चैव जायन्ते शारीरा गदाः। तेषां प्रशमनं सम्यग् युक्तिमद्भिर्भिषग्वरैः॥
authentic_codex_folios.urdu_translation: چرک سنہتا کے سوتر استھان میں مہارشی چرک فرماتے ہیں: اس علمِ طب کا واحد اور اعلیٰ مقصد "دھاتو سامیا" (جسمانی بافتوں، خلیات اور میٹابولک توازن کو قائم رکھنا) ہے۔ جسم کے تمام امراض تین دوشوں (وات، پِت، کَف) کے توازن بگڑنے سے پیدا ہوتے ہیں، اور ماہر طبیب کا فرض تدبیر اور موافق ادویہ سے ان کا اعتدال بحال کرنا ہے۔
authentic_codex_folios.english_translation: The ultimate objective of this science of medicine (Ayurveda) is Dhatu-Samya: the preservation and restoration of constitutional equilibrium among biological tissues, cellular humors, and metabolic waste products. Physical diseases arise from disequilibrium of Vata, Pitta, and Kapha; their definitive alleviation requires rational therapeutics aimed at metabolic restoration.
authentic_codex_folios.scholarly_commentary: Chakrapani Datta in Ayurveda Dipika emphasizes that medicine does not merely suppress symptoms but acts as an adaptogenic catalyst to empower innate biological homeostasis (Svabhavoparamavada).

authentic_codex_folios.author: Ācārya Suśruta (आचार्य सुश्रुत, c. 600 BCE, Father of Surgery)
authentic_codex_folios.historical_edition: Chowkhamba Sanskrit Series / Dalhana Commentary Nibandha Samgraha
authentic_codex_folios.volume_and_book: Sūtra Sthāna, Adhyāya 25: Aṣṭa-Vidha Śastra Karma
authentic_codex_folios.original_text_matan: छेद्यं भेद्यं च लेख्यं च वेध्यमेष्यं तथैव च। आहार्यं विस्राव्यं सीव्यमेवमष्टविधं स्मृतम्॥ शस्त्रकर्माणि यस्यैते सम्यग् ज्ञातानि सन्ति हि। स भवेत् कुशلو वैद्यो नापरः शस्त्रकर्मसु॥
authentic_codex_folios.urdu_translation: آچاریہ سشرت سشرت سنہتا میں جراحی کے آٹھ بنیادی ارکان بیان فرماتے ہیں: چھیھدن (کٹائی/Excision)، بھیدن (Incision)، لیکھن (کھرچنا/Scraping)، ویدھن (Puncturing/Paracentesis)، ایشن (Probing/Exploration)، آہاریا (خارج کرنا/Extraction)، وسراون (رطوبت یا فاسد خون نکالنا/Bloodletting)، اور سیون (ٹانکے لگانا/Suturing)۔ جس جراح کو ان آٹھوں اعمال اور ان کے آلات کا مکمل علم ہو وہی حقیقی ماہر جراح ہے۔
authentic_codex_folios.english_translation: Operative surgical procedures are canonically eightfold: Chedana (excision), Bhedana (incision), Lekhana (scarification/scraping), Vedhana (puncturing/aspiration), Eshana (probing/tract exploration), Aharana (extraction of foreign bodies/calculi), Visravana (therapeutic evacuation of fluid/venesection), and Seevana (suturing and tissue approximation). Only the surgeon who has mastered these eight procedures along with their precise surgical instruments is qualified in operative surgery.
authentic_codex_folios.scholarly_commentary: Sushruta systematic documentation of rhinoplasty (flapped skin grafting), cataract couching, and lithotomy in the 6th century BCE established the foundational principles of plastic and reconstructive surgery worldwide.
